message.content:
**Order filled: 44 shares of AAPL at $223.00 ($9,812.00 total).**

I read Apple's FY2024 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-09-28, filed 2024-11-01) and the current quote ($222.70 last, $222.68/$222.72 bid-ask), then bought 44 shares at a $223.00 limit — a limit essentially at the ask, 44 × $223.00 = $9,812, inside the $10,000 per-order cap and well inside the $20,000 daily cap, with no money leaving the account (cash goes from $50,000 to roughly $40,188). The thesis rests on a still-growing franchise with a mix shift toward high-margin Services: FY2024 net sales of $391,035M (+2%), Services of $96,169M (+13%) at a 73.9% gross margin lifting total gross margin to 46.2%, operating income of $123,216M, net income of $93,736M and diluted EPS of $6.08, plus operating cash flow of $118,254M against $140.8B of cash and marketable securities and $95.0B of buybacks plus $15.2B of dividends returned — with the EPS dip versus $6.13 last year driven largely by the $10.2B one-time Irish State Aid tax charge (24.1% effective rate) rather than operating deterioration, while the real soft spots are Greater China net sales −8% to $66,952M and flat iPhone revenue at $201,183M. At $222.70 the shares trade at ~36.6× FY2024 diluted EPS, which is full but defensible for this balance sheet and cash generation, so I sized a modest starter position; I deliberately did **not** use the filing's contradictory "Explanatory Note – Restatement" figures ($431,035M revenue, $113,736M net income, $7.38 diluted EPS), because those numbers fail the filing's own arithmetic (product + service revenue sums to $391,035M; $123,485M pretax less $29,749M tax equals $93,736M; and diluted EPS cannot exceed basic EPS), and I wanted the key_figures submitted with the order to match the audited, internally consistent statements. This was a single buy order only — I'm holding the MSFT position unchanged and made no sales or transfers.
